title: MathTutorBench: A Benchmark for Measuring Open-ended Pedagogical Capabilities of LLM Tutors
learner_level: middle/high school math learners as represented in source datasets
tutoring_capabilities: problem solving; Socratic questioning; student solution correctness; mistake location; mistake correction; scaffolding generation; pedagogical instruction following
human_expert_role: teacher-created dialogue data; expert teacher revisions; human annotations/preference data from related datasets
rubric_or_metric: task-specific metrics; reward model for scaffolding score; win rate against teacher responses
reliability_evidence: reward model distinguishes expert vs novice teacher responses; reported comparisons in Section 6.2
main_findings: Problem-solving expertise does not directly translate to pedagogical tutoring ability; longer dialogues are harder; pedagogical preference data matters.
limitations: focuses on math tutoring; does not replace learning-outcome studies; limited long dialogues; safety not fully covered
relevance_to_project: Strong evidence for separating correct-answer ability from tutoring quality and for including student-understanding/scaffolding tasks.
evidence_location: Abstract; Section 3.2; Section 4; Table 1; Table 2; Section 6; Limitations
reviewer_notes: support_label summary: direct evidence for solver-vs-tutor separation, student understanding, scaffolding; inference for serious-error policy.

title: From Solver to Tutor: Evaluating the Pedagogical Intelligence of LLMs with KMP-Bench
tutoring_capabilities: holistic pedagogical dialogue; follow-up problem solving; error detection and correction; problem generation; Challenge; Explanation; Modelling; Practice; Questioning; Feedback
human_expert_role: human-crafted few-shot examples; manual verification of dialogue flows; human expert annotation for evaluator validation
rubric_or_metric: general criteria; principle-specific criteria; Win/Tie/Lose comparison; accuracy/F1/MR-score for skills; LLM evaluator alignment with manual labels
reliability_evidence: reports 89.8% alignment rate between LLM evaluator and human ground truth on a subset; Table 3
main_findings: LLMs can solve verifiable tasks yet struggle with nuanced pedagogical principles; pedagogically rich data improves tutoring performance.
limitations: K-8 math domain; synthetic generation plus verification; many criteria may be heavy for a small pilot
relevance_to_project: Strong evidence for evaluating pedagogical intelligence and for human verification of dialogue soundness/sequencing.
evidence_location: Abstract; Figure 1; Evaluation Framework; Table 1; Table 2; Table 3; Main Results
reviewer_notes: support_label summary: direct evidence for solver-to-tutor distinction, principle-based evaluation, human verification; inference for compact rubric grouping.

title: TutorBench: A Benchmark To Assess Tutoring Capabilities Of Large Language Models
tutoring_capabilities: adaptive explanation; assessment and feedback; active learning support; student-level calibration; guiding questions; misconception identification; step-by-step help
task_or_dataset: TutorBench; 1,490 samples; text-only and multimodal tutoring scenarios
human_expert_role: subject experts write questions, golden responses and rubrics; human-expert ratings validate LLM judge
rubric_or_metric: sample-specific rubrics; pass/fail criteria; weights +5/+1/-5; weighted average ARRw; rubric tags; Bloom analysis
reliability_evidence: human expert ratings on 250 samples / 2,475 criteria; LLM judge agreement and F1 reported in Section 3.7
main_findings: Frontier LLMs remain below 56%; adaptive explanation is difficult; Bloom level does not map linearly to model performance; model weaknesses vary by tutoring skill.
limitations: high-school/AP STEM not Vietnamese THCS; evaluates final response in pre-formulated conversations; LLM judge validation may not transfer to Vietnamese Tin học 9
relevance_to_project: Strong evidence for three tutor use cases, sample-specific observable criteria, expert authoring and careful LLM-judge validation.
evidence_location: Section 2.1; Section 2.3; Section 2.4; Section 3.4; Section 3.5; Section 3.7; Section 5; Appendix A.1
reviewer_notes: support_label summary: direct evidence for tutor use cases, rubric construction, Bloom caution and judge validation; inference for compact rubric mapping.
